ordered_diagnoses: Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome (Gorlin Syndrome)
Basal Cell Carcinoma with SUFU Mutation

facts.raw_span: multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored asymptomatic papules located on the face and vulva
The lesions first appeared around 50 years of age and gradually increased to approximately 60 lesions
Medical history was significant for a meningioma
Family history was notable for a daughter with similar facial papules that had not undergone biopsy
No palmar or plantar pits were observed
buds and cords of basaloid cells enclosing small cystic spaces
Clefting between tumor aggregates and the surrounding stroma was focally evident
Radiographic studies did not reveal any jaw cysts
A conserved splice-site mutation in SUFU gene (c.757-2A>G) in all tumor and normal tissue samples
Additional distinct deletions of the trans SUFU allele in all tumor samples
No deletions present in the normal sample

concepts.preferred_label: Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome (Gorlin Syndrome)
concepts.why: The patient's presentation of multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules, history of meningioma, and family history of similar facial papules, along with the genetic mutation in the SUFU gene, are all consistent with Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome (Gorlin Syndrome).

The histopathological features of the patient's lesions, including buds and cords of basaloid cells enclosing small cystic spaces and clefting between tumor aggregates and the surrounding stroma, are characteristic of infundibulocystic basal cell carcinoma.

concepts.preferred_label: Basal Cell Carcinoma with SUFU Mutation
concepts.why: The patient's tumors and normal tissue samples both showed a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene, which is a known genetic mutation associated with basal cell carcinoma.
The patient's family history of similar facial papules and the presence of a genetic mutation in the SUFU gene suggest a familial component to the patient's basal cell carcinoma.

Although the patient did not have any radiographic evidence of jaw cysts, the presence of basal cell carcinomas and a family history of similar lesions raises the possibility of odontogenic keratocysts.
The patient's medical history of meningioma is a known association with Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome (Gorlin Syndrome).
The patient's presentation of multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules is consistent with basal cell carcinoma, although the presence of other features suggests a more specific diagnosis.
The patient's family history of similar facial papules and the presence of a genetic mutation in the SUFU gene suggest a genetic predisposition to skin cancer.

concepts.preferred_label: SUFU-related multiple keratocysts and basal cell carcinomas
concepts.why: The presence of a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene and additional distinct deletions of the trans SUFU allele in all tumor samples, with no deletions in the normal sample, explains the uncovered fact of genetic alterations in the patient's condition.
